COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   B. Remove all guards
   C. Work alone with eyes closed
   D. Run with the tool

2. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   B. Ignore burnt cables
   C. Overload every socket
   D. Never touch live wires with wet hands

3. When learning Binary Arithmetic Operations, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Binary Arithmetic Operations.

4. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. Information and Communication Technology
   D. Input Cable Tester

5. When learning Network Security, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Network Security.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Network Security.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Security.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Network Security.

6. When learning Structured Query Language, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Structured Query Language.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Structured Query Language.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Structured Query Language.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Structured Query Language.

7. When learning Object Oriented Programming Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.

8. When learning Web Development Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Web Development Fundamentals.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Web Development Fundamentals.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Web Development Fundamentals.

9. When learning Computer Network Standards and Protocols, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.

10. When learning Logic Circuits, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Logic Circuits.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Logic Circuits.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Logic Circuits.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Circuits.

11. When learning Data Representation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Representation.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Representation.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Representation.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Data Representation.

12. When learning Object Oriented Programming Implementation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Logic Circuits and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Computer Network Standards and Protocols and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Network Security and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Object Oriented Programming Concepts and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

2. D — Never touch live wires with wet hands

3. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Binary Arithmetic Operations.

4. C — Information and Communication Technology

5. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Security.

8. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.

10. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Circuits.

11. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Representation.

12. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
